extracted.intended_audience: students and practitioners of rhetoric; writers, law and MFA students
extracted.subtask_description: Classical-rhetoric guidance for composing and evaluating prose, covering narrative modes, figures/tropes, the five canons, and style levels. Useful for writers, rhetoricians, and students learning how verbal devices and arrangement determine effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fictitious (Mythos)
rubrics_metrics.description: The fully invented — found in tragedies and poems. No requirement of factual truth; truth is artistic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when the work is wholly invented; evaluate fitness by artistic truth rather than factual accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Realistic (Argumentum)
rubrics_metrics.description: What is not true but could be true — comedy. Maintains verisimilitude.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply to fiction that aims to seem possible; judge by plausibility and internal consistency appropriate to realistic narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical (Historia)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exposition of actual fact. The rhetorician should begin training here, 'whose force is in proportion to its truth.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used for factual accounts; evaluate based on fidelity to fact and the persuasive weight that truth lends the discourse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metaphor
rubrics_metrics.description: Trope: implicit comparison (one word substitutes another to suggest likeness).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess clarity and aptness of comparison; whether the metaphor illuminates rather than obscures meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metonymy
rubrics_metrics.description: Trope: substitution by association (using something closely related to stand for the thing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate appropriateness of associative link and whether it tightens expression or creates confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synecdoche
rubrics_metrics.description: Trope: part for whole (using a component term to refer to the whole).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for economy and evocative power; ensure the part/whole relation is clear to the audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antonomasia
rubrics_metrics.description: Trope: epithet for name (using a descriptive phrase or title instead of a proper name).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge felicity of substitution and whether it adds rhetorical punch or distracts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Onomatopoeia
rubrics_metrics.description: Trope: sound mimicking sense (words that imitate natural sounds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess sensory vividness and appropriateness to tone—can be vivid but risk triviality if overused.

rubrics_metrics.name: Catachresis
rubrics_metrics.description: Trope: strained metaphor (sometimes a fault).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat as potentially faulty usage; determine if the strained comparison creates striking effect or mere awkwardness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allegory
rubrics_metrics.description: Trope: extended metaphor (systematic substitution across a work).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate coherence of the extended mapping and whether it supports the work's meaning rather than overwhelming it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyperbole
rubrics_metrics.description: Trope: exaggeration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge degree and purpose of exaggeration—effective for emphasis, problematic if it undermines credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Litotes
rubrics_metrics.description: Trope: affirmation by negation of contrary (understatement by denying the opposite).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess subtlety and effect; can lend irony or understatement when used deliberately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periphrasis
rubrics_metrics.description: Trope: circumlocution (roundabout phrasing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether circumlocution enriches nuance or needlessly obscures meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Irony
rubrics_metrics.description: Trope: saying the opposite of what is meant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate clarity of ironic stance and alignment with audience expectations; poor signaling can lead to misunderstanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apostrophe
rubrics_metrics.description: Figure of thought: direct address (addressing an absent person or personified thing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to create immediacy or emotional emphasis; assess whether it fits the rhetorical situation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antithesis
rubrics_metrics.description: Figure of thought: opposition (contrasting ideas placed in parallel).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge balance and clarity of contrast; effective for sharpening argument or heightening style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aporia
rubrics_metrics.description: Figure of thought: feigned doubt (pretended uncertainty as a rhetorical device).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess strategic use to invite reflection or distance the speaker; avoid overuse that signals indecision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Praeteritio
rubrics_metrics.description: Figure of thought: mentioning by saying you won't mention (pretending to pass over a point while bringing it up).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate subtlety and ethical implications—can be rhetorically powerful but manipulative if abused.

rubrics_metrics.name: Erotema (Rhetorical question)
rubrics_metrics.description: Figure of thought: rhetorical question (asking without expecting an answer).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge its ability to engage the audience and focus thought; avoid hollow or rhetorical filler.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anaphora
rubrics_metrics.description: Figure of thought: repetition at start of clauses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess rhythmic and emphatic effects; repetition should amplify meaning rather than become monotonous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Epistrophe
rubrics_metrics.description: Figure of thought: repetition at end of clauses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate cumulative emphasis and sound pattern; ensure the repeated element remains meaningful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chiasmus
rubrics_metrics.description: Figure of thought: reversed parallelism (ABBA structure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge elegance and clarity of inversion; effective in creating memorable phrasing when logically sound.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asyndeton
rubrics_metrics.description: Figure of thought: omission of conjunctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess briskness and intensity produced by omission; risk of confusion if coordination is unclear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polysyndeton
rubrics_metrics.description: Figure of thought: addition of conjunctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge cumulative or solemn effect created by repetition of conjunctions; can slow rhythm intentionally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventio (finding what to say)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the Five Canons: discovering arguments and material to use in discourse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate richness and appropriateness of material generated; foundation for persuasive force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dispositio (arranging it)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the Five Canons: ordering material for maximum effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess logical structure, progression, and emphasis—order should enhance clarity and persuasion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elocutio (style; word choice; figures)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the Five Canons: the choice of language and rhetorical ornament.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge diction, figures, and appropriateness of language to purpose and audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memoria (memorization)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the Five Canons: the art of memory in rhetorical performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider role where oral delivery is relevant; memorability of phrasing contributes to rhetorical success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pronuntiatio (delivery)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the Five Canons: physical delivery and vocal presentation of speech.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When performance matters, evaluate tone, pace, gesture, and vocal clarity as part of rhetorical effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain style
rubrics_metrics.description: Style level: for instruction; minimal ornament.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when clarity and didacticism are primary aims; excess ornament is a fault here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Middle style
rubrics_metrics.description: Style level: for pleasure; balanced between plain and grand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for elegance without excess—suitable for pleasing prose that still informs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grand style
rubrics_metrics.description: Style level: for moving the audience; full rhetorical resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deploy when the goal is to elevate or move readers; requires mastery to avoid bombast.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of narrative mode and fitness
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluative axis: identify whether the piece is fictitious, realistic, or historical and whether that mode is appropriate to the matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A failure occurs when the wrong mode is invoked for the matter; judge coherence between subject matter and chosen narrative mode.

rubrics_metrics.name: Catalog of tropes and figures employed
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluative axis: inventory which tropes and figures the prose uses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Quintilian's terminology to precisely describe verbal techniques; exhaustive catalog helps diagnose strengths and weaknesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whether figures serve meaning or merely decorate
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluative axis: determine if rhetorical figures contribute to meaning or only ornament the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer figures that are integral to sense and argument; decorative figures without purpose are weaknesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style level and modulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluative axis: determine the work's style level (plain/middle/grand) and whether the writer skillfully modulates among levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A skilled writer modulates among the three styles within a single work; judge appropriateness of shifts and overall tonal control.
